title: Migration platform: pure planning logic (Plan, pending, sequence validation)
prompt:
Build the pure planning logic of the schema migration platform test-first, in package `mongodb` at backend/internal/platform/mongodb. Leave the existing mongodb.go (Connect, Ping) as it is. This task has no MongoDB access, so everything here is unit-testable without a server. The platform package must not import any bounded context (internal/archtest enforces this).

Ubiquitous language (put it in the doc comment of migration.go):
- Migration: one forward-only, numbered schema change. It has an ID `<context>/<NNNN>` (e.g. `catalog/0001`), a Description and an Up step.
- Migration set: all migrations of one bounded context, in sequence order.
- Ledger: the `schema_migrations` collection, which records each applied migration.
- To migrate: to apply all pending migrations in order.
Rules: migrations are forward-only and have no down step; a mistake is fixed by a new migration. Within a context, sequence numbers start at 0001 and have no gaps or duplicates. Each context migrates independently of the others.

Contract. Other tasks build against exactly these names, some of them in parallel with you:
```go
// Migration is one forward-only, numbered schema change of one bounded context.
type Migration struct {
    ID          string // "<context>/<NNNN>", e.g. "catalog/0001"
    Description string
    Up          func(ctx context.Context, db *mongo.Database) error
}

var (
    ErrInvalidMigrationSet = errors.New("invalid migration set")
    ErrUnknownMigration    = errors.New("unknown migration in ledger")
)

// Plan validates the migration sets and returns all migrations in apply order:
// the sets in the given order, each one in sequence order. It never touches the database.
func Plan(sets ...[]Migration) ([]Migration, error)

// pendingMigrations returns the migrations of plan whose ID is not in applied, in plan order.
func pendingMigrations(plan []Migration, applied []string) ([]Migration, error)
```
`mongo` is go.mongodb.org/mongo-driver/v2/mongo. This task only stores Up and never calls it.

Plan rules. Every violation returns an error that wraps ErrInvalidMigrationSet and names the offending migration ID (or context):
- The ID must match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*/[0-9]{4}$`. Sequence 0000 is invalid.
- The Description must not be blank, and Up must not be nil.
- All migrations of one set share the same context. A context may appear in only one set.
- An empty set is allowed (a context that has no migrations yet).
- Within a set, detect and report these cases separately, checking them in this order:
  1. a duplicate sequence number (`duplicate`);
  2. a sequence number lower than its predecessor (`out of order`);
  3. a sequence that doesn't run 0001, 0002, ... without holes, including a first number other than 0001 (`gap`).
- Plan returns a new slice and never modifies its input.

pendingMigrations: if applied contains IDs that plan doesn't know (an older binary on a newer database), return an error that wraps ErrUnknownMigration and names every unknown ID, sorted. Example: `unknown migration in ledger: catalog/0003 (the database is newer than this binary)`. Otherwise return the not-yet-applied migrations in plan order. applied may come in any order.

Tests go in migration_test.go (`package mongodb`), table-driven, with no MongoDB. Cover:
- Plan: a valid single set; several sets (check the apply order); an empty set; each kind of malformed ID; a blank description; a nil Up; mixed contexts; a context registered twice.
- Sequence checks: one case each for a duplicate, a gap (both a hole and a set that starts at 0002) and out-of-order numbers. Assert errors.Is(err, ErrInvalidMigrationSet) and that the message contains the ID.
- pendingMigrations: nothing applied; everything applied; only the newest pending; applied IDs in random order; unknown IDs (errors.Is ErrUnknownMigration, and the message names the ID).

Coordination:
- Another task writes ledger.go, lock.go, schema.go and testdb_test.go in the same package at the same time.
- A later task writes migrate.go, whose Migrate calls Plan and then pendingMigrations.
- Only create migration.go and migration_test.go.
- Give any extra unexported helpers specific names, also in the test file (e.g. parseMigrationID, planTestUp), so nothing collides when the two tasks merge.

backend/check.sh must pass.

title: Migration platform: ledger, schema lock (lease) and validator/index helpers
Migration platform: Migrate (lock, renew, apply, record, log)
prompt:
Build Migrate, the schema migrator that ties the migration platform together. It goes in backend/internal/platform/mongodb/migrate.go (package mongodb), with tests in migrate_test.go. It runs at server startup when STORAGE=mongo.

Domain rules (from the story):
- To migrate is to apply all pending migrations in order: the sets in the given order, each set in sequence order. Each context migrates independently.
- Migrations are forward-only. A migration is applied at most once, and it is recorded in the ledger (`schema_migrations`) only after its Up step succeeded.
- If the ledger contains a migration ID the running code doesn't know (an older binary on a newer database), refuse with an error naming that ID.
- Only one instance migrates at a time. Others wait for the schema lock, then re-check the ledger. The lock expires if its holder dies (lease of at most 60 s, renewed while migrating).
- If a migration fails, Migrate returns an error naming its ID, and the server doesn't start.
- Each applied migration is logged with its ID, description and duration.

Already in the package and merged (read the code):
- migration.go:
  - `type Migration struct { ID, Description string; Up func(ctx context.Context, db *mongo.Database) error }`
  - `ErrInvalidMigrationSet`, `ErrUnknownMigration`
  - `func Plan(sets ...[]Migration) ([]Migration, error)`
  - `func pendingMigrations(plan []Migration, applied []string) ([]Migration, error)`
- ledger.go:
  - `LedgerCollection`
  - `type ledgerEntry struct { ID (bson _id), Description, AppliedAt time.Time, DurationMs int64 }`
  - `appliedMigrationIDs(ctx, db) ([]string, error)`
  - `recordMigration(ctx, db, ledgerEntry) error`
- lock.go:
  - `LockCollection`, whose one document is {_id: "schema", owner, expiresAt}
  - `ErrSchemaLockLost`
  - `newSchemaLock(db, owner, lease) *schemaLock`, with `tryAcquire`, `acquire(ctx, poll)`, `renew` and `release`
- schema.go: `EnsureCollection`, `EnsureIndexes`.
- testdb_test.go: `newTestDB(t) *mongo.Database`. It skips without MONGO_TEST_URI and gives each test its own database.

Contract. Bootstrap, the e2e tests and the docs use exactly this:
```go
const (
    DefaultLease        = 30 * time.Second
    MaxLease            = 60 * time.Second
    DefaultPollInterval = 500 * time.Millisecond
)

// MigrateOptions tunes Migrate; the zero value uses the defaults.
type MigrateOptions struct {
    Lease        time.Duration // schema lock lease; 0 = DefaultLease; > MaxLease is an error
    PollInterval time.Duration // wait between lock attempts; 0 = DefaultPollInterval
    Owner        string        // lock owner; "" = hostname plus random hex (crypto/rand)
    Logger       *slog.Logger  // nil = slog.Default(), looked up at call time
}

// Migrate applies all pending migrations of sets to db, in order.
func Migrate(ctx context.Context, db *mongo.Database, sets [][]Migration, opts MigrateOptions) error
```

Algorithm:
1. Validate the options and call Plan(sets...). Return any error before touching the database; db may even be nil at this point.
2. Read the ledger and call pendingMigrations. If there are unknown IDs, return that error. If nothing is pending, return nil without taking the lock, so restarts stay lock-free.
3. Acquire the schema lock with acquire(ctx, PollInterval). It waits while another live instance holds the lock.
4. Start a renewal goroutine that calls renew every Lease/3. If renew fails (ErrSchemaLockLost or any other error), cancel the migration context with that error as the cause. Stop the goroutine and wait for it before releasing the lock.
5. Re-read the ledger under the lock and recompute what's pending; another instance may have migrated while we waited. Unknown IDs are an error here too.
6. For each pending migration:
   a. If the migration context is cancelled (the lock was lost), stop with an error naming the migration.
   b. Run Up with the migration context, and time it.
   c. If Up fails, return `fmt.Errorf("schema migration %s failed: %w", m.ID, err)` without recording anything.
   d. Otherwise record a ledgerEntry, with AppliedAt = the time Up finished (UTC) and DurationMs.
   e. Log at Info with message `schema migration applied` and attributes `id`, `description` and `durationMs` (int64).
7. Always release the lock, also after failures, with a context that survives cancellation of ctx: context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 5*time.Second).

Unit tests (no MongoDB):
- Migrate(ctx, nil, sets, opts) with a duplicate, a gap or an out-of-order set returns ErrInvalidMigrationSet without panicking, which proves nothing touched the database.
- A Lease greater than MaxLease is rejected.

Integration tests use newTestDB and synthetic sets with IDs catalog/0001, catalog/0002, ... whose Up steps count their calls with atomic counters. Use short leases and polls. Cover:
- On an empty database, all migrations run in order, and each one is in schema_migrations with appliedAt and durationMs.
- When every migration is already applied, running again runs nothing.
- When catalog/0002 is added to the set, only catalog/0002 runs.
- When catalog/0002 fails: the error names catalog/0002, it isn't recorded, and catalog/0001 stays recorded. After the fix, Migrate applies only catalog/0002.
- Two Migrate calls with different owners at the same time on an empty database both return nil, and every Up runs exactly once.
- A lock document left by a dead instance ({_id: "schema", owner: "dead", expiresAt: now+1s}): Migrate waits for the lease to expire, then takes the lock and migrates.
- A migration slower than the lease (lease 1 s, Up sleeps about 2.5 s): renewal keeps the lock, so a second instance started meanwhile doesn't run it concurrently. Each Up runs exactly once, and two Ups are never in flight at the same time.
- The ledger contains catalog/0003 but the set only knows up to catalog/0002: errors.Is(err, ErrUnknownMigration), the message names catalog/0003, and no Up ran.
- The lock document is gone after a success and after a failure.
- With a Logger that writes to a buffer, each applied migration is logged with id, description and durationMs.
If MONGO_TEST_URI is set in your environment, these tests must pass.

Scope: only migrate.go and migrate_test.go. If you find a bug in lock.go, ledger.go or migration.go, don't edit those files. Describe the bug in your final message and propose a fix in .orch-proposals.json. backend/check.sh must pass.

title: Catalog context: books collection schema as migration catalog/0001
prompt:
Add the first consumer of the schema platform: the storage schema of the `catalog` bounded context, as migration catalog/0001. It goes in package `mongodb` at backend/internal/catalog/adapter/mongodb/, which is a new context.

This story adds only the schema: no domain, app, repository or HTTP code. Those come in the next story, built on this schema. Don't touch bootstrap; S01-05 wires this in.

Platform API you build on. It lives in package orch-test/backend/internal/platform/mongodb; import it as `platformmongo`, because this package is also named mongodb.
```go
type Migration struct { ID string; Description string; Up func(ctx context.Context, db *mongo.Database) error }
func Plan(sets ...[]Migration) ([]Migration, error) // validates a set; the error wraps ErrInvalidMigrationSet
func EnsureCollection(ctx context.Context, db *mongo.Database, name string, jsonSchema bson.D) error // validator {$jsonSchema}, strict/error; create or collMod; idempotent
func EnsureIndexes(ctx context.Context, db *mongo.Database, collection string, models ...mongo.IndexModel) error // every model needs a name; idempotent
```

Contract:
```go
const BooksCollection = "books"
// Migrations is the catalog context's migration set, in sequence order.
func Migrations() []platformmongo.Migration // [{ID: "catalog/0001", Description: "create books collection with validator and indexes", Up: ...}]
```
The Up step of catalog/0001 calls EnsureCollection(books, schema) and then EnsureIndexes(books, ...). Say in the doc comment that future changes are new migrations (catalog/0002, ...) appended to Migrations(), and that an applied migration is never edited.

The `books` collection holds one document per book. Every field is validated, and any field not listed is rejected. Build the $jsonSchema with bson.D and bson.A throughout, so the order is deterministic:
- Top level: bsonType object; additionalProperties: false (so `_id` must be listed in properties); required: [_id, isbn, title, authors, createdAt, updatedAt, version].
- `_id`: bsonType long. It is the int64 book ID, assigned later from a counters document {_id: "books", seq}. This migration doesn't create the counter.
- `isbn`: string, pattern ^97[89][0-9]{10}$ (ISBN-13: exactly 13 digits, starting with 978 or 979). The domain validates the check digit later; the database doesn't.
- `title`: string, minLength 1, maxLength 300.
- `authors`: array, minItems 1, maxItems 20; each item is a string with minLength 1 and maxLength 200.
- `publishedYear`: int (int32), minimum 1450, maximum 2100. Optional.
- `language`: string, pattern ^[a-z]{2}$ (ISO 639-1). Optional.
- `pages`: int (int32), minimum 1, maximum 10000. Optional.
- `createdAt`, `updatedAt`: date. Required.
- `version`: long (int64), minimum 1. Required, for optimistic concurrency.

Indexes:
- `isbn_unique`: {isbn: 1}, unique.
- `authors_lookup`: {authors: 1}, for lookups by author.

Tests, written test-first:
- Unit test (no MongoDB): Plan(Migrations()) succeeds, and the IDs are exactly [catalog/0001].
- Integration tests run only when MONGO_TEST_URI is set and call t.Skip otherwise. Each test uses its own database test_<random hex>, dropped in t.Cleanup; write a small newTestDB helper in this package's tests.
- Run every Up step of Migrations() in order, then insert documents directly with the driver.
- Use explicit Go types: int64 for _id and version, int32 for publishedYear and pages, time.Time for dates. A plain Go int would encode as int32 and fail bsonType long.
- Assert failures precisely, so a case can't pass for the wrong reason: a validation failure is a mongo.WriteException with code 121 (DocumentValidationFailure), and the duplicate ISBN is detected with mongo.IsDuplicateKeyError.

Cover the story's criteria:
- A complete, valid book is accepted, and so is one with only the required fields.
- A book without isbn, title, authors, createdAt, updatedAt or version is rejected (one case per field).
- An isbn with 12 or 14 digits, with letters or hyphens, or starting with 977 is rejected.
- A second book with an existing isbn is rejected (unique index).
- An empty title, a 301-character title, an empty authors array, 21 authors, or an empty author name is rejected. A 300-character title, 20 authors and a 200-character author name are accepted.
- publishedYear 1449 or 2101, pages 0 or 10001, and language `EN` or `eng` are rejected. The bounds 1450, 2100, 1 and 10000 and the language `en` are accepted.
- A document with an extra field (e.g. price) is rejected. So are wrong types: an int32 _id, and version 0.
- The isbn (unique) and authors indexes exist.
- Running the Up step a second time succeeds and changes nothing.
If MONGO_TEST_URI is set in your environment, these tests must pass.

backend/check.sh must pass. archtest allows this adapter to import the platform package and the driver, and nothing from other contexts.

title: Hardening review: schema migration platform and books schema
prompt:
Do a hardening review of story S-01. In scope:
- the MongoDB schema migration platform: backend/internal/platform/mongodb (migration.go, ledger.go, lock.go, schema.go, migrate.go);
- the catalog/0001 books schema (backend/internal/catalog/adapter/mongodb);
- its wiring in backend/internal/bootstrap and the startup path in backend/cmd/server;
- docker-compose.yml and backend/Dockerfile.
Write the report to docs/security/S01-08-schema-migrations.md. No API endpoints changed in this story. Authentication and authorization, including MongoDB authentication, are out of scope: list them once as an accepted risk for local dev.

How it works: with STORAGE=mongo, bootstrap.New calls mongodb.Migrate before building the server. Migrate:
1. validates the migration sets (Plan);
2. reads the ledger schema_migrations ({_id: migration ID, description, appliedAt, durationMs}) and refuses unknown IDs (ErrUnknownMigration);
3. takes a lease lock in schema_lock ({_id: "schema", owner, expiresAt}; default lease 30 s, at most 60 s, renewed every lease/3);
4. applies the pending migrations, then records and logs each one.

title: Document the schema migration platform and the books collection
prompt:
Document the schema migration platform for backend developers in docs/schema-migrations.md. Read the code and document what exists:
- backend/internal/platform/mongodb (migration.go, ledger.go, lock.go, schema.go, migrate.go);
- backend/internal/catalog/adapter/mongodb (catalog/0001);
- backend/internal/bootstrap/bootstrap.go (migrationSets, and the Migrate call in New).

Keep it concise and skimmable. Cover:
- Glossary:
  - migration: an ID `<context>/<NNNN>`, a description and an Up step;
  - migration set;
  - ledger: schema_migrations, with _id, description, appliedAt and durationMs;
  - schema lock: a lease in schema_lock, at most 60 s, renewed while migrating;
  - validator: $jsonSchema, with validationLevel strict and validationAction error;
  - migrate.
- Rules:
  - Migrations are forward-only; there are no down migrations, and a mistake is fixed with a new migration.
  - Each context numbers its migrations from 0001, without gaps or duplicates.
  - A migration is applied at most once, and recorded only after it succeeded.
  - An unknown ID in the ledger stops startup.
  - One instance migrates at a time.
  - The server serves HTTP only after the migrations finished.
  - STORAGE=memory migrates nothing and doesn't connect to MongoDB.
- How to add a migration to a context:
  - Add or extend func Migrations() in internal/<context>/adapter/mongodb, appending the next number.
  - Use EnsureCollection and EnsureIndexes. They are idempotent, but an index definition can't be changed in place.
  - Register a new context's set in bootstrap's migrationSets.
  - Never edit an applied migration.
  - Include a short Go example modelled on catalog/0001.
- Typing pitfalls: a Go int encodes as BSON int32, so use int64 for long fields such as _id and version.
- The books collection: the field table (types and rules) and the two indexes, as implemented.
- Operations:
  - what the startup log shows;
  - what to do when startup fails: a failing migration, an unknown ledger ID from an older binary, or a lock left by a dead instance (it expires after its lease);
  - how to run the MongoDB tests: make test-mongo, MONGO_TEST_URI, one database per test.
